title: Burst Delegation and Epochal Fallback — design notes (PRD WIP)
summary: Sketch for a coordinated burst delegation mechanism that lets tenants borrow short-lived capacity across epoch windows, with deterministic fallback paths and hard-isolation boundaries. Focused on predictable latency SLOs while enabling controlled opportunistic bursting and fast autoscaling for sustained demand.
background: Customers using Dedicated pools want predictable baseline capacity but also need to absorb traffic spikes without manual reserve purchases. Current approaches (hard reserves or blunt throttles) either increase cost or cause customer-visible failures. We need a system that mixes predictable commitments with controlled, accountable bursting and safe fallback semantics.
goals: 1) Allow tenants to safely borrow capacity for short spikes without breaking other tenants' SLOs. 2) Ensure burst borrowing is bounded, auditable, and reversible. 3) Provide deterministic fallback policies (model variant fallback, regional failover, degraded-quality lane). 4) Expose observability and billing signals for each burst event.
non_goals: 1) This PRD does not design long-term capacity forecasting or pricing model changes. 2) Not addressing on-prem air-gapped installation specifics (handled in private deployments team). 3) Not covering model-level quantization or kernel-level optimizations.
proposal: Introduce a Burst Delegation Controller (BDC) that operates at the pool level and coordinates short epoch windows (configurable: 30s, 2m, 15m). Tenants have two balances: committed units (reserved slots) and burst credits (ephemeral). The BDC manages: - allocation of ephemeral slots when pool headroom exists, - admission policy based on SLO-weighted priority, - ledgering of burst usage for billing and forgiveness, - enforcement of isolation via soft fences and hard caps.
autoscaling_design: Autoscaler will operate with three signals: 1) steady-state queue depth and token rate, 2) short-window latency p99 regressions, 3) burst-exhaustion events from BDC. When short-window demand increases, BDC may grant ephemeral slots first (cheap, fast) before scaling up. If ephemeral slots exceed a tenant's burst cap or pool headroom is low, autoscaler kicks in with prewarm and fast-scale policies (targeted nodes + warm KV cache replication). Autoscaler modes: conservative (low churn), opportunistic (aggressive prewarm), and emergency (rapid add + degraded routing). Each mode maps to SLA tiers.
burst_delegation: Key primitives: - epoch_window: atomic time slice for delegation decisions. - burst_cap: tenant-configured max ephemeral concurrency per epoch. - delegation_token: opaque token issued to tenant on successful ephemeral grant (used for traceability). - grace_credit: small overcommit allowance to absorb microbursts. Delegation flow: request arrives -> admission checks (tenant priority, recent SLO violations, current headroom) -> issue delegation_token if approved -> charge ledger. Delegation is revocable: a revocation notice includes remaining TTL allowing callers to gracefully degrade (e.g., switch model variant). Revocation paths: soft revoke (no immediate eviction, reduce new admission), hard revoke (preempt provisional slots).
isolation_controls: Isolation is multilayer: 1) Soft fences: admission policies, rate-aware queueing, priority lanes. 2) Hard caps: absolute concurrency per-tenant and pool-wide safety caps. 3) Tenant shaping: token bucket per-tenant with burst window tied to delegation_epoch. 4) Noisy-neighbor detection: continuous scoring based on token consumption, latency impact, and error rates; high score triggers automated quarantine (temporary stricter caps + owner notification). Quarantine runbook includes mitigation steps and automatic cooldown.
telemetry_and_alerting: Events to emit: delegation_grant, delegation_revoke, delegation_denied, burst_quota_exhausted, preemptive_scale, quarantine_start/stop. Metrics: per-tenant ephemeral_concurrency, delegation_tokens_issued, epoch_violation_count, p99_latency_by_tenant, headroom_ratio, autoscale_actions. Alerts: repeated revocations for a tenant (>=3 within 10m), pool headroom < 10% for > 2m, quarantine events. Dashboards: per-pool timeline with annotated delegation events and autoscaler actions.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (canary): implement BDC prototype in staging, route small set of internal tenants (dev & partner teams), collect telemetry and adjust admission heuristics. Phase 1 (limited beta): enable for paid dedicated customers with explicit opt-in and conservative burst caps. Phase 2 (general availability): default opt-in for dedicated with per-tenant safe defaults; provide console controls for caps and billing opt-out. Rollback: immediate disable of BDC (revert to pure autoscale + throttle) is supported by a feature flag.
open_questions: 1) How should burst credits be priced and reconciled with committed billing? 2) Exact epoch defaults and tradeoffs (short epochs reduce latency but increase control churn). 3) How to compose delegation across regional pools (cross-region borrowing). 4) UX for tenants to visualize and request temporary cap increases.
dependencies: Autoscaler service changes (autoscale v2), runtime admission hooks (serving-runtime team), console controls (product-console), billing pipeline changes. Security review for delegation tokens. QA: chaos testing for revocation paths.
